newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates ease at close, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates ease at close, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistan's inter-bank money market rates closed lower after opening up on Tuesday amid a shortage of funds but are likely to rise on Wednesday because of a central bank open market operation, dealers said.
Overnight funds were initially traded at 19 percent but desperate borrowing pushed the rates up to the 20 percent mark, a dealer at KASB & Co said.
Heavy trading was conducted in the range of 19.50 and 19.95 percent, but the borrowing pressure eased near close bringing the rates down to 17 percent, the dealer said.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has an open market operation for Wednesday, which may absorb an inflow of one billion rupees expected on maturity of papers sold in an earlier market operation, dealers said.
